rules.name: Security Deposit Return (15 Days / 30 Days Claim)
rules.statuteSummary: Landlord has 15 days to return the deposit together with interest if not imposing a claim. If imposing a claim for damages, landlord has 30 days to give written certified notice of intention. Landlords who fail to send notice forfeit the right to impose a claim.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under Fla. Stat. § 83.49(3)(a), a landlord has 15 days to return the deposit if no claim is made, or 30 days to provide certified written notice of specific itemized deductions. Longer timeframes in the lease are void.

rules.name: Notice of Entry for Repairs (24 Hours Notice - Miya's Law)
rules.statuteSummary: Under Fla. Stat. § 83.53(2), as amended by Miya's Law (SB 898), reasonable notice for entry for repairs is statutorily defined as at least 24 hours prior notice (between 7:30 a.m. and 8:00 p.m.). The landlord may enter at any time without notice only in an emergency. Lease provisions providing less than 24 hours notice or waiving notice are legally non-compliant.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under Fla. Stat. § 83.53(2) (as amended by Miya's Law, SB 898), reasonable notice for entry to perform repairs is mandatory at least 24 hours prior to entry between 7:30 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. Provisions demanding entry with 12 hours or less, or waiving notice, violate Florida law.

rules.name: Prohibited Practices (Self-Help Eviction & Utility Shutoff)
rules.statuteSummary: A landlord of any dwelling unit shall not cause the termination or interruption of any utility service, prevent tenant from gaining reasonable access by changing locks, or remove outside doors or tenant personal property. Violators are liable for actual damages or 3 months' rent, whichever is greater.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under Fla. Stat. § 83.67, self-help evictions, changing locks, and cutting off utilities are prohibited practices carrying statutory damages of three months' rent plus attorney's fees.

rules.name: Landlord Duty to Maintain Premises (Non-Waivable Habitability)
rules.statuteSummary: Under Fla. Stat. § 83.51, the landlord shall at all times during the tenancy comply with the requirements of applicable building, housing, and health codes, maintaining roofs, windows, doors, floors, steps, and plumbing in reasonable repair. Under Fla. Stat. § 83.47, any provision in a rental agreement that purports to waive or preclude tenant rights or remedies under Chapter 83 is void and unenforceable.
rules.disputeTemplate: Under Fla. Stat. § 83.51 and § 83.47, landlord duties to maintain the premises in compliance with applicable building, housing, and health codes cannot be waived by lease terms. Clauses transferring structural maintenance duties or waiving habitability are void under Florida law.
